newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Unidentified gunmen kidnap 11 Bangladesh tribals.
newsitem.headline: Unidentified gunmen kidnap 11 Bangladesh tribals.

text.p: Eleven villagers in Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts, site of a long-running tribal insurgency, have been abducted by unidentified gunmen, local officials said on Wednesday.
They said the 11, all local tribespeople, had been forced at gunpoint from their homes in the Bandarban hill district on Tuesday and taken into the nearby jungle.
"Their whereabouts have not been known since," one police officer told reporters on Wednesday.

Police said they did not know who the abductors were, but villagers speculated that they could be members of the Shanti Bahini, a tribal guerrilla group fighting for autonomy for the Hill Tracts, or rebels from west Burma, which borders Bandarban.
"It still remains a puzzle," one police officer said.
The government is currently in peace talks with the Shanti Bahini, which began their insurgency in 1973 in the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts bordering India and Burma.
Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, government soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, which has forced up to 50,000 tribespeople to flee to northeast India.
Security sources said Burmese rebels have been known to cross into the Hill Tracts to team up with the Shantis, often collecting money from villagers.
